summary: We have only been discussing and consumed with high level preoccupations  over troops levels, drowned down timelines, surges and sting operations  when we should be examining the details of where the social fabric  has been most torn, where the community has improvised  and survived and show acts of resilience and amazing courage  just to keep life going.

We are missing the story of Faridah,  a music teacher, a piano teacher in Sarajevo  who made sure that she kept the music school open  every single day in the four years of the siege in Sarajevo  and walked to that school despite the sniper shooting  at that school and at home  and kept the piano, the violin, the cello playing the whole duration of the war  with students wearing their gloves and hats and coats.

We are missing the story of Nhaia,  a Palestinian woman in Gaza  who the minute there was a ceasefire last in the last year's war  she left out of home, collected all the flowers  and baked as much bread for every neighbor to have  in case there is no ceasefire the day after.

A Congolese woman who was telling me about how  her children saw their father killed in front of them  and saw her raped in front of them  and mutilated in front of them  and their children saw their nine year old sibling killed in front of them  how they are doing okay right now  she got into women's home and international programs  she got a support network she learned about her rights  we taught her vocation on business skills  we helped her get a job  she was earning $450 she was doing okay  she's sending them to school have a new home  she said but what I worry about the most is not any of that  I worry that my children have hate in their hearts  and when they want to grow up  they want to fight again  the killers of their father and their brother  we need to invest in women  because that's our only chance  to ensure that there is no more war in the future  that mother has a better chance to heal her children  than any peace agreement can do  are there good news?

that girl that I told you about  and an upstanding woman from an international group  that impacted 1 million people  sent $80 million  and I started this from zero nothing  not a real issue  there are women who are standing on their feet  in spite of their circumstances  not because of it  think of how the world can be a much better place  if for a change  we have a better equality  we have equality  we have a representation  and we understand war  both from the front line  and the back line discussion  Rumi, a 13th century super poet  says, out beyond the worlds  of right doings and wrong doings  there is a field  I will meet you there  when the soul lies down in that grass  the world is too full to talk about  ideas, language  even the phrase each other  no longer makes any sense  I humbly add  humbly add  that out beyond the worlds of war  and peace  there is a field  and there are many women and men  are meeting there  let us make this field a much bigger place  let us all meet in that field  thank you  that was Zainab Salbi  recorded at TED Global 2010  in Oxford, England, July 2010  for more information on TED  visit TED.com
